newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes drift to higher close in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes drift to higher close in thin trade.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed up 30 basis points at 29.50 percent on Friday after a slow session, traders said.
"Overnight rates did not waver much and volume was thin again," said a trader.
Traders said that rates were not under great upside pressure, but rather small trades had an exaggerated effect at low volume.
Traders said the market was listless as most dealers were already evaluating strategies for next year.
"Events that had led to uncertainty are over for the time being, and most dealers are busier drawing up their strategies for next year," said a money market analyst.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed unchanged at 31.00 percent.
Banco de Mexico injected 2.11 billion pesos by auctioning one credit which it assigned at 31.03 percent.
Traders said they expected short-term Cetes rates to decline at Monday's primary auction due to recent peso stability.
The auction will be held one day early next week, as the week will be cut in half by the anniversary of the Mexican Revolution on November 20.
Credit maturities for Monday were estimated at 5.031 billion pesos.
